verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents a first-party CLI, `fhcli`, built for submitting changes from existing CI or orchestration systems such as Jenkins deploys and CI build statuses. Headless automation is also covered by a token-authenticated API that can do anything the UI can, plus bot tokens for non-human callers. Both parts of the story, headless operation and CI automation, are documented by the product itself. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of CI usage, and documentation showing `fhcli` can do more than record change and deploy events (broader CI-driven automation relies on the raw API).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: FireHydrant provides a command line tool, `fhcli`, to easily submit changes from your existing CI or orchestration systems.
You can use fhcli to record the creation of Docker images, deploy events in Jenkins, CI build statuses, etc.
You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.
FireHydrant allows you to access the API with an API key using token-based authentication.
FireHydrant supports bot tokens to act on behalf of a computer instead of a user's account.
